equipment.overview: Arborist equipment is the backbone of safe climbing, rigging, and cutting. Every piece of gear has a specific purpose, a weight rating, and a correct method of use. Professional climbers rely on gear discipline — inspecting, maintaining, and understanding every component before leaving the ground.

harness.description: Your harness is your foundation. It supports your hips, distributes weight, and anchors your lifeline, lanyard, and gear loops. Arborist harnesses include side D-rings, a central bridge, and multiple attachment points.
harness.safety: Always inspect stitching, bridge wear, D-ring integrity, and buckles before climbing.

lifeline.description: Your lifeline rope is your main climbing system. It must be static or semi-static, 11–13mm, and rated for arborist use.
rules: Retire ropes with glazing, cuts, or core shots.

carabiners.description: Carabiners must be triple-lock, auto-lock, and rated for climbing.
carabiners.warnings: Never use cheap aluminum carabiners for climbing or rigging.

lanyards.description: Your lanyard is your second point of safety. Used for positioning, flips, and stability.

ascenders.description: Ascenders help you climb rope efficiently.

frictionDevices.description: Friction devices control descent, movement, and rigging friction.

spikes.description: Spikes are ONLY for removals. They damage live trees.
rules: Never spike a tree you are pruning.
Strap spikes tight to avoid rotation.
Use proper foot placement to avoid gaff-out.

helmets.description: Helmets must be arborist-rated with chin straps.
helmets.protection: Protects from falling limbs, saw kickback, slips, and impacts.

gloves.description: Gloves protect your hands from rope burn, cuts, and abrasion.

saws.description: Chainsaws must be sharp, well-maintained, and used with PPE.

pulleys.description: Pulleys reduce friction and redirect loads.

slings.description: Slings attach hardware to trees safely.

ropeCare.description: Rope must be kept clean, dry, and away from chemicals.

ratings.description: Every piece of gear must be rated for climbing.
